info.title: OTK Server APIs
info.description: All API's available in OAuth Toolkit server

get.description: Initializes an OAuth 2.0 flow using a response_type. See RFC 6749 (https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6749) for more details.

parameters.name: mag-identifier
parameters.description: The mag-identifier is used in conjunction with response_type 'code'.  This field is required for Mobile clients. It must represent a valid registered mobile device. A client is identified as a mobile client if its registered SCOPE includes 'msso'.

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: This is the 'client_id' of the requesting client. Maximum 255 characters.

parameters.name: response_type
parameters.description: MUST be one of the listed available values. Any response_type other than 'code' or 'token' is only supported in conjunction with scope=openid. As per the OAuth specification: 'code' is used for authorization code grant type flow, 'token' is used for implicit grant type flow, 'token id_token' is an extension provided by OpenID Connect, and 'code id_token', 'id_token', and 'none' are extensions provided by OpenID Connect Multiple Response Types

parameters.name: response_mode
parameters.description: Specify the method of returning the authorization response. As per the OpenID specification, use of this parameter is NOT RECOMMENDED if you are using the same response mode as the default response mode for the given response type. It MUST be one of the listed values in order to be accepted: 'query', 'fragment', 'form_post'.

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description: The 'redirect_uri' that was registered for this client. It is required if multiple redirect_uri's have been registered for this client. If the scope contains openid, this field becomes MANDATORY.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Only SCOPE values that were registered for this client will be granted. If only non-matching SCOPE values are requested, the request will fail.

parameters.name: nonce
parameters.description: This is required for response_type 'token id_token'.  Typically, in an OpenID authorization scheme, the nonce represents a cryptographically strong random  string that is used to prevent intercepted responses from being reused.

parameters.name: display
parameters.description: This is optional and used within the context of OpenID Connect (ie, response_type 'token id_token'). This parameter is not used here but forwarded to the /authorize/login API. Currently only 'page', 'social_login' (MAG only) and 'local' (MAG only) are supported by default. The value 'social_login' will create a JSON message response instead of an HTML page containing a list of social login providers. The value 'local' will prevent the authorization server from displaying the social login buttons. This is the case if a user selected the local enterprise button for logging in.

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.description: This is used within the context of OpenID Connect. Indicates whether the server should prompt for login/consent. It is a space separated list of different values. The server supports the values 'none', 'login' and 'consent'. 'none' is only respected if 'id_token_hint' is not empty. 'consent' is only respected if the current user has an active OAuth session using the same client and the same SCOPE.

parameters.name: id_token_hint
parameters.description: This is used within the context of OpenID Connect. Contains a previously issued id_token. This parameter is only respected for 'prompt=none' or 'prompt=none consent'.

parameters.name: acr_values
parameters.description: This is used within the context of OpenID Connect. Indicates which acr (additional cryptography) classes are acceptable for the user authentication. It is a space separated list of different values.

parameters.name: code_challenge
parameters.description: The code_challenge value in the context of PKCE (RFC 7636).

parameters.name: code_challenge_method
parameters.description: The method that was used to create the code_challenge (plain or S256).

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Value opaque to the server, used by the client to track its session. It will be returned as received.

parameters.name: login_hint
parameters.description: A suggested username. This parameter is described in the OpenID Connect core specification.

location.description: Location (URL) includes these required parameters: action=(display or login depending on 'prompt' and 'id_token_hint') & sessionID & sessionData (a JWT containing a JSON message holding session data)

400.description: Invalid parameters | Invalid redirect_uri | invalid client type | invalid response type | invalid code_challenge/method

get.description:
This API reflects an implementation according to OpenID Connect. This endpoint returns a message with user details. The content depends on the SCOPE associated with the given access_token.
IMPORTANT: The API will fail if no active id_token is available for the associated user.
For more information refer to this website: http://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#UserInfo

parameters.name: authorization
parameters.description: A valid access_token (e.g.: authorization: Bearer access-token-value). The access_token must have the 'openid' scope. Other valid scope values are 'email', 'address', 'phone', and 'profile'. In addition to those scope values, 'user_role' is supported. The 'user_role' scope is an extension for OTK/MAG and returns the role of the user.

200.description: A JSON message containing details about the user. The content depends on the scope associated with the access_token.

x-ca-err.description: Custom error header. Possible value: 134

error_description.example: The request did not match CORS requirements

get.description: An endpoint that can be used to verify your OAuth authentication flow is working correctly. Is only usable if the context variable otk.health.apikey is defined inside the corresponding service policy.

parameters.name: apikey
parameters.description: Key that needs to be used to perform health check.

500.description: Responds with "error". This can be due to missing or incorrect API key. Check audit log messages for more information.

503.description: Responds with "error". Returned on health check failure. This can be returned due to bad database configuration, bad certification configuration, etc. Check the audit log messages for more information.

location.description:
If 'action' is 'grant': the redirect location will include the query parameters: state(if provided) and code.  In the 'implicit' response flow, the query parameters include: redirect_uri, access_token, expires_in, token_type, scope, id_token, id_token_type and state.  
If 'action' is 'deny':  the redirect will location include the 'x-ca-err', 'error', 'error_description' and 'state' (if provided) parameters.  In such a case the 'error' is 'access_denied'

parameters.name: grant_type
parameters.description: For grant_type=password either authorization or client_id AND client_secret, username and password must be provided. For grant_type=client_credentials, either authorization or client_id AND client_secret must be provided. For grant_type=authorization_code: client_id, client_secret, code, and redirect_uri are required. For grant_type=refresh_token: client_id and refresh_token are required. For grant_type=jwt or saml2-bearer: client_id and assertion are required

parameters.description: If grant_type is password or client_credentials, this parameter must contain a valid password

parameters.name: assertion
parameters.description: If grant_type is saml2-bearer or jwt, this parameter must contain a base64 encoded SAML or JWT token that represents an authenticated resource owner.

parameters.name: refresh_token
parameters.description: If grant_type is refresh_token, this parameter must contain a valid refresh_token.

parameters.name: code_verifier
parameters.description: A random value of 43-256 characters. See https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7636#section-4 for details.  This parameter is required only when a code_challenge is provided with the authorization request for this session.

x-ca-err.description: Custom error extension, possible values:  3010134 (request did not match CORS requirements)

get.description: This endpoint implements the JWKS_URI as specified at http://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-discovery-1_0.html#ProviderMetadata

200.description: JWK set containing public keys that enable clients to validate a JSON Web Token (JWT) issued by this OpenID Connect Provider

keys.description: JWK set in JSON array format

x-ca-err.description: Custom error extension. Possible values: 3010203 (SSL required)

405.description: The HTTP method is not valid

Allow.description: This header is required by RFC 2616 and contains a comma separated list of valid HTTP methods.

x-ca-err.description: Custom error extension

export200.description: A JSON message including details about a client in order to configure it. The client_secret may or may not be included depending on the OAuth server configuration.

auth302.description: Will contain either: A success response including the redirect location header to the server that handles the authentication.  The redirect parameter 'sessionData's structure looks like the model schema shown OR 'invalid mag-identifier' OR 'invalid scope' OR 'unsupported response type' OR 'unauthorized client'. The non-successful conditions may include redirect query params as follows: 'error', string with default value:  invalid_request 'error_description', string with description of error 'state', string with no default value.  It is opaque to the server and returned as received. 'x-ca-err', string with default 3000108

location.description: Location (URL) includes these required parameters: action=(display or login depending on 'prompt' and 'id_token_hint') & sessionID & sessionData (a JWT containing a JSON message holding session data)

authToken200.description: A success response that includes the issued token, expire and other details from the OAuth Server

access_token.description: The Access Token for the given token request

id_token.description: If the requested SCOPE included 'msso' or 'openid', response includes an id_token

id_token_type.description: If the requested SCOPE included 'msso' or 'openid', response includes an id_token_type

organization.description: A session ID, matching the sessionID

scope.description: The scopes available for the client

redirect_uri.description: The registered redirect_uri for the client

registered_by.description: The id of the entity that registered the client

sessionID.description: A session ID, matching the sessionID

userinfo_endpoint.description: URL of the user info endpoint

jwks_uri.description: URL of JSON Web Key Set document

scopes_supported.description: list of the OAuth 2.0 scope values that this server supports

subject_types_supported.description: list of the Subject Identifier types that this OP supports

token_endpoint.description: URL of the OAuth 2.0 token endpoint

id_token_signing_alg_values_supported.description: list of the JWS signing algorithms (alg values) supported by the OP for the ID Token to encode the Claims in a JWT

response_types_supported.description: ist of the OAuth 2.0 response_type values that this OP supports

claims_supported.description: list of the Claim Names of the Claims that the OpenID Provider MAY be able to supply values for

authorization_endpoint.description: URL of the OAuth 2.0 authorization endpoint

issuer.description: the identifier of the token's issuer. This is identical to the 'iss' Claim value in ID Tokens

grant_types_supported.description: list of the OAuth 2.0 Grant Type values that this OP supports

acr_values_supported.description: list of the Authentication Context Class References that this OP supports

token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported.description: list of Client Authentication methods supported by this Token Endpoint

token_endpoint_auth_signing_alg_values_s.description: list of the JWS signing algorithms (alg values) supported by the Token Endpoint for the signature on the JWT used to authenticate the Client at the Token Endpoint for the private_key_jwt and client_secret_jwt authentication methods. Servers SHOULD support RS256. The value none MUST NOT be used.

display_values_supported.description: list of the display parameter values that the OpenID Provider supports

claim_types_supported.description: list of the Claim Types that the OpenID Provider supports

service_documentation.description: URL of a page containing human-readable information that developers might want or need to know when using the OpenID Provider

ui_locales_supported.description: Languages and scripts supported for the user interface

OpenIDDiscovery.description: The OpenID configuration document as defined by the specification: http://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-discovery-1_0.html#ProviderMetadata
